questions.stem: A condensation polymer is formed from a dicarboxylic acid and a diol. What small molecule is released during this polymerisation, and what linkage is formed?

options.text: Carbon dioxide is released; an amide linkage forms
Water is released; an ester linkage forms
Hydrogen is released; a C-C bond forms
Oxygen is released; an ether linkage forms

questions.explanation: When a dicarboxylic acid (-COOH groups) reacts with a diol (-OH groups), water (H₂O) is eliminated from each pair of reacting functional groups, forming ester linkages (-COO-). This is why it is called condensation polymerisation — a small molecule (water) is released as a by-product, unlike addition polymerisation where no by-product forms.

questions.stem: Nylon is a condensation polymer made from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine. What type of linkage holds the monomers together in nylon?

options.text: Ester linkages (-COO-)
Ether linkages (-O-)
Amide linkages (-CONH-), also called peptide bonds
Carbon-carbon single bonds

questions.explanation: When a -COOH group from the dicarboxylic acid reacts with a -NH₂ group from the diamine, water is released and an amide linkage (-CONH-) forms. These are the same type of bonds found in proteins (where they are called peptide bonds). Nylon's amide linkages give it strength and the ability to form fibres.

questions.stem: PET (polyethylene terephthalate) is a polyester used to make drinks bottles. Unlike addition polymers, PET can be chemically recycled by hydrolysis. What does hydrolysis of a polyester produce?

options.text: The original alkene monomers
The original dicarboxylic acid and diol monomers
Carbon dioxide and water
Smaller polymer chains only

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis is the reverse of condensation — water breaks the ester linkages, regenerating the original monomers (dicarboxylic acid and diol). This is an advantage of condensation polymers over addition polymers: they can be broken down into their monomers for reuse. This is a form of chemical recycling that is more sustainable than landfill.

questions.stem: A student tries to make a condensation polymer using a monomer with only one -OH group and one -COOH group. Can this monomer polymerise?

options.text: No, because condensation polymerisation requires two different monomers
Yes — a monomer with both -OH and -COOH can react with itself to form a polyester chain
No, because only addition polymerisation can use a single monomer
Yes, but it will form an addition polymer instead

questions.explanation: A monomer with both a -COOH and -OH group (like a hydroxy acid) can undergo self-condensation. The -COOH of one molecule reacts with the -OH of another, forming ester linkages and releasing water. This produces a polyester from a single type of monomer. Polylactic acid (PLA), a biodegradable plastic made from lactic acid, works exactly this way.

questions.stem: Both polyesters and nylon are condensation polymers, but nylon is much stronger and is used for ropes and climbing gear. What structural feature gives nylon its extra strength?

options.text: Nylon has C=C double bonds in its backbone
The amide (-CONH-) linkages in nylon can form hydrogen bonds between chains, creating a stronger material
Nylon has shorter chains than polyester
Nylon is a metal alloy, not a polymer

questions.explanation: The N-H group in nylon's amide linkages can form hydrogen bonds with the C=O group of adjacent chains. These hydrogen bonds between polymer chains create strong intermolecular forces, making nylon fibres very strong and tough. Polyesters have ester linkages (-COO-) which cannot form as many hydrogen bonds, so they are generally less strong.
